announcements.title: VerusMiner v6 is here 🎉
announcements.description: CPU-specific builds (ca53, ca78, kryo, …), in-app build recommendation, Mining power, overnight Keep mining connected. Releases on GitHub.
announcements.content:
VerusMiner v6 is here

Thanks for mining with us. Version 6 is a big step forward for Verus Coin phone mining. CPU-specific optimized builds with in-app recommendations, smarter mining power profiles, better overnight reliability, clearer stats, and less battery drama when you set things up once.

What's new

New 37 CPU-specific optimized miner builds

VerusMiner includes new set of CPU-tuned miner binaries — one optimized build per core type. Each build is identified by a short tag such as ca53, ca78, or kryo (same naming pattern as the previous versions).

These builds are fast with huge improvements compared to the previous versions.

All short tags (quick index)

gen, ca34, ca35, ca53, ca55, ca57, ca65, ca65ae, ca72, ca73, ca75, ca76, ca76ae, ca77, ca78, ca78c, ca78ae, ca510, ca520, ca710, ca715, ca720, ca725, cr82, cx1, cx1c, cx2, cx3, cx4, cx925, nve1, nvn1, nvn2, nvn3, nvv1, nvv2, nvv3, thunderx, thunderx2t99, tsv110, apa7, apa10, apa14, apm1, ampere1, ampere1a, a64fx, kryo, exm3, exm4, exm5, falkor, saphira

Supported specific builds (tag → CPU)

Generic

  • gen — generic

ARM Cortex-A (efficiency / mid)

  • ca34 — cortex-a34
  • ca35 — cortex-a35
  • ca53 — cortex-a53
  • ca55 — cortex-a55
  • ca57 — cortex-a57
  • ca65 — cortex-a65
  • ca65ae — cortex-a65ae
  • ca510 — cortex-a510
  • ca520 — cortex-a520

ARM Cortex-A (performance)

  • ca72 — cortex-a72
  • ca73 — cortex-a73
  • ca75 — cortex-a75
  • ca76 — cortex-a76
  • ca76ae — cortex-a76ae
  • ca77 — cortex-a77
  • ca78 — cortex-a78
  • ca78c — cortex-a78c
  • ca78ae — cortex-a78ae
  • ca710 — cortex-a710
  • ca715 — cortex-a715
  • ca720 — cortex-a720
  • ca725 — cortex-a725
  • cr82 — cortex-r82

ARM Cortex-X

  • cx1 — cortex-x1
  • cx1c — cortex-x1c
  • cx2 — cortex-x2
  • cx3 — cortex-x3
  • cx4 — cortex-x4
  • cx925 — cortex-x925

ARM Neoverse

  • nve1 — neoverse-e1
  • nvn1 — neoverse-n1
  • nvn2 — neoverse-n2
  • nvn3 — neoverse-n3
  • nvv1 — neoverse-v1
  • nvv2 — neoverse-v2
  • nvv3 — neoverse-v3

Other (Kryo, Exynos, server, Apple, …)

  • thunderx — thunderx
  • thunderx2t99 — thunderx2t99
  • tsv110 — tsv110
  • apa7 — apple-a7
  • apa10 — apple-a10
  • apa14 — apple-a14
  • apm1 — apple-m1
  • ampere1 — ampere1
  • ampere1a — ampere1a
  • a64fx — a64fx
  • kryo — kryo
  • exm3 — exynos-m3
  • exm4 — exynos-m4
  • exm5 — exynos-m5
  • falkor — falkor
  • saphira — saphira

Notes: On mixed big.LITTLE phones the in-app recommender prefers the faster cores (and will not pick kryo over a stronger ARM big core when both are present). Unknown CPUs fall back to gen.

Build recommendation (new)

You no longer need to guess which binary fits your phone. VerusMiner will give you the best recommendation:

  • Open Device Info (stop mining first)
  • Run Detect CPU topology / review the build suggestion card
  • The app maps your CPU parts to the short tags above (e.g. Cortex-A53 → ca53) and suggests the best build — plus other on-device matches and gen as a safe try list
  • Compare fairly: run each candidate a similar duration and watch hashrate and temperature
  • After switching a build or Mining power profile, restart mining so the new binary and settings apply

Optimized mining (Mining power)

Stop guessing thread counts. Mining power profiles map to how modern phones work (big.LITTLE cores, heat, and battery):

  • Balanced — everyday mining with about half your cores; good hashrate without cooking the phone
  • Performance — prefers the faster cores when your device has them, for higher hashrate when plugged in and cooled
  • Cooler — fewer cores than Balanced so the phone stays cooler and the battery lasts longer (great overnight or in warm rooms)
  • Custom — full manual control of threads and pause limits when you want to tune further

Profiles can also apply comfort pauses: auto-pause on high temperature or low battery, then resume after a cooldown — so mining protects the hardware instead of thrashing until it throttles.

Overnight connection & network tips (Keep mining connected)

Mining that dies when the screen turns off is usually the phone sleeping Wi‑Fi or killing the app — not the pool. Use Keep mining connected in Settings before long or overnight sessions:

  • Battery unrestricted / don’t optimize VerusMiner — stop Android from killing the miner in the background
  • Wi‑Fi stays on when the screen is off (Wi‑Fi sleep policy “Never” on older phones) — or use solid mobile data if that is more reliable on your network
  • Turn off aggressive power saving modes that cut CPU or network overnight
  • Check OEM “battery savers”, auto-kill / sleep apps, and game/boost modes that break long sessions
  • Prefer a stable 2.4 GHz or wired-router Wi‑Fi near the device; avoid captive portals and flaky guest networks
  • Do not swipe VerusMiner away from Recents while mining — that kills the process
  • Use temperature and battery pause limits (or Cooler profile) so overnight heat or low charge pauses cleanly instead of hard disconnects
  • Optional: game/performance modes when supported, for steadier clocks during the session

Tip: plug in for multi-hour runs, pick Cooler or Balanced, finish Keep mining connected once per phone model, and leave space for airflow. If shares stop overnight, re-check Wi‑Fi sleep and battery unrestricted first.

History and graphs

  • Session history with ranges (1h to 30d)
  • Live charts while mining: hashrate, temperature, shares, difficulty
  • When mining stops, home can still show your last session graphs so you can review what worked
  • History and miner setting used can now be saved paired with complete graphs so you can compare performance based on real-world data for every run

Smoother mining UX

  • Clearer home and bottom navigation
  • Accepted/hour and other metrics that are easier to read
  • Notice if the app was force-closed while mining (so you know why it stopped)
  • Refreshed onboarding and Quickstart for first-time setup
  • Mining screen UI is improved with additional stats for acceptance rate per hour and realtime pool accepted hashrate
  • Warning is added for using the default Verus Coin Foundation wallet address. This is to warn users from claiming coins that they do not own and more importantly to save everyones' time

Custom Mining Pool / Stratum

  • Creation of custom stratum is now supported
  • You can now add custom stratum pool that will appear in the stratum selection when creating miner setting

Look and language

  • Multiple themes (including community styles)
  • More languages via refreshable language packs

Speed test and Network debug

  • Speed test feature is refined. Fastest pinged pool goes to the top first
  • Network debug feature is added to enable user to check the network status during mining. This saves everyone a lot of headache especially when debugging

VerusBox Compatibility

  • VerusBox is still compatible especially the local monitoring and remote control feature
  • VerusBox will have a new version release too, so stay tuned

Online Monitoring is back

  • MyVerusMiners is the successor of the VersuMonitor web app
  • VerusMiner app is configured to automatically connect to MyVerusMiners so you can view your miners while you're away
  • Access https://my-verusminers.pangz.space/ or from your VerusMiner app
  • MyVerusMiners is and will always be free to use

Tips after updating

  • Open Device Info → detect CPU topology (stop mining first)
  • Install the suggested short-tag build (e.g. ca78) from GitHub if an upgrade is recommended
  • Try Mining power: Balanced daily, Performance when plugged in, Cooler overnight
  • Open Keep mining connected and finish battery + Wi‑Fi items for each phone
  • Refresh languages/themes if you want the latest remote packs

Download and details

Use the button below or open the GitHub releases page for notes and downloads.

Happy hashing — and thank you for supporting the Verus Coin community.
